question_text: The reaction: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{OH}$ is a/an:
explanation: Tertiary butyl bromide reacts with water via a nucleophilic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}1$) mechanism where the $-\text{OH}$ group replaces the $-\text{Br}$ leaving group to form *tert*-butyl alcohol.

question_text: $\text{CH}_3-\text{Mg}-\text{Br}$ is an organometallic compound due to:
explanation: An organometallic compound contains a direct covalent/polar-covalent bond between a carbon atom of an organic group and a metal atom; in methylmagnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$), this is the $\text{C}-\text{Mg}$ bond.

question_text: On mixing a certain alkane with chlorine and irradiating it with ultraviolet light, it forms only one monochloroalkane. This alkane could be:
explanation: In neopentane ($(\text{CH}_3)_4\text{C}$), all twelve hydrogen atoms belong to four equivalent primary ($1^\circ$) methyl groups, so free-radical monochlorination yields only a single monochloroalkane, neopentyl chloride ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{Cl}$).

question_text: The compound formed on heating chlorobenzene with chloral in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid is:
explanation: Heating two equivalents of chlorobenzene with chloral ($\text{CCl}_3\text{CHO}$) in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields $p,p'$-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, commonly known as DDT.

question_text: Elimination of bromine from 2-bromobutane results in the formation of:
explanation: Dehydrobromination of 2-bromobutane follows Saytzeff's rule, giving the more substituted, thermodynamically more stable alkene—2-butene—as the major product.

question_text: Alkyl halides react with dialkyl copper reagents to give:
explanation: Dialkyl lithium cuprates (Gilman reagents, $\text{R}_2\text{CuLi}$) couple with alkyl halides ($\text{R}'\text{X}$) via cross-coupling to form higher alkanes: $\text{R}_2\text{CuLi} + \text{R}'\text{X} \longrightarrow \text{R}-\text{R}' + \text{R}\text{Cu} + \text{LiX}$.

question_text: Reaction of one molecule of $\text{HBr}$ with one molecule of 1,3-butadiene at $40^\circ\text{C}$ gives predominantly:
explanation: At higher temperature ($40^\circ\text{C}$), addition of $\text{HBr}$ to 1,3-butadiene is under thermodynamic control, yielding the more stable internal disubstituted alkene, 1-bromo-2-butene (1,4-addition product), predominantly.

question_text: Tertiary alkyl halides are practically inert to substitution by $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism because of:
explanation: An $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction requires backside nucleophilic attack on the $\alpha$-carbon; three bulky alkyl groups on a tertiary carbon block this approach through severe steric hindrance.

question_text: 2-Methylbutane on reacting with bromine in the presence of sunlight gives mainly:
explanation: Free-radical bromination is highly selective and proceeds via the most stable carbon radical intermediate. In 2-methylbutane, abstraction of the tertiary ($3^\circ$) hydrogen gives the most stable $3^\circ$ radical, forming 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product.

question_text: Reaction of *trans*-2-phenyl-1-bromocyclopentane on reaction with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ produces:
explanation: Concerted $\text{E}_2$ dehydrobromination requires an *anti*-periplanar arrangement of the leaving group ($-\text{Br}$ at C-1) and the $\beta$-hydrogen. In *trans*-2-phenyl-1-bromocyclopentane, the $\beta$-H at C-2 is *cis* to $-\text{Br}$ and cannot achieve an *anti*-periplanar geometry, so elimination occurs at C-5 to form 3-phenylcyclopentene.

question_text: The structure of the major product formed in the reaction of 1-chloromethyl-2-chlorobenzene (or *o*-chlorobenzyl chloride) with $\text{NaCN}$ in $\text{DMF}$ is:
explanation: The benzylic $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond readily undergoes nucleophilic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}2$) with $\text{CN}^-$ in $\text{DMF}$ to give the nitrile (*o*-chlorobenzyl cyanide), whereas the vinylic/aryl $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond on the aromatic ring does not undergo substitution under these conditions.

question_text: $\text{CH}_3\text{Br} + \text{Nu}^- \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{Nu} + \text{Br}^-$. The decreasing order of the rate of the above reaction with nucleophiles ($\text{Nu}^-$) A to D is [where $\text{Nu}^- = (\text{A})\;\text{PhO}^-, (\text{B})\;\text{AcO}^-, (\text{C})\;\text{HO}^-, (\text{D})\;\text{CH}_3\text{O}^-$]:
explanation: For oxygen nucleophiles attacking $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$, nucleophilicity correlates with basicity: $\text{CH}_3\text{O}^-(\text{D}) > \text{HO}^-(\text{C}) > \text{PhO}^-(\text{A}) > \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-(\text{B})$ (since carboxylate resonance delocalises negative charge over two oxygens more strongly than phenoxide delocalises it into the ring).

question_text: $\text{HBr}$ reacts with $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{OCH}_3$ under anhydrous conditions at room temperature to give:
explanation: Electrophilic addition of $\text{HBr}$ across the alkene double bond occurs regioselectively to form the resonance-stabilised $\alpha$-alkoxycarbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}^+-\text{OCH}_3 \leftrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{O}^+\text{CH}_3$), followed by capture of $\text{Br}^-$ to give $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CHBr}-\text{OCH}_3$.

question_text: The structure of the compound that gives a tribromo derivative on treatment with bromine water is:
explanation: Phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) is strongly activated towards electrophilic aromatic substitution and reacts rapidly with excess bromine water to form a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol (whereas *o*- and *p*-cresols already have one *ortho* or *para* position blocked by $-\text{CH}_3$).

question_text: Fluorobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{F}$) can be synthesized in the laboratory:
options: from aniline by diazotisation followed by heating the diazonium salt with $\text{HBF}_4$
by direct fluorination of benzene with $\text{F}_2$ gas
explanation: Fluorobenzene is prepared via the Balz-Schiemann reaction by diazotising aniline to benzenediazonium chloride, precipitating the diazonium fluoroborate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{BF}_4^-$) with $\text{HBF}_4$, and thermally decomposing it to $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{F}$.

question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of decreasing $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactivity? ($\text{X} = \text{a halogen}$)
explanation: $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactivity decreases as steric hindrance around the $\alpha$-carbon increases: primary ($1^\circ$, $\text{RCH}_2\text{X}$) $>$ secondary ($2^\circ$, $\text{R}_2\text{CHX}$) $>$ tertiary ($3^\circ$, $\text{R}_3\text{CX}$).

question_text: Which of the following reactions will yield 2,2-dibromopropane?
explanation: Propyne ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$) undergoes two successive Markovnikov additions of $\text{HBr}$: first giving 2-bromopropene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}=\text{CH}_2$) and then 2,2-dibromopropane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}_2-\text{CH}_3$).

question_text: The organic chloro compound, which shows complete stereochemical inversion during a $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction, is:
explanation: Among the given compounds, $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ has the least steric hindrance and undergoes $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ backside attack most readily (as given in the official answer key).

question_text: Which of the following on heating with aqueous $\text{KOH}$, produces acetaldehyde?
explanation: 1,1-Dichloroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHCl}_2$, a *gem*-dihalide) reacts with aqueous $\text{KOH}$ to form an unstable *gem*-diol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}_2$, which loses a molecule of water to yield acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$).

question_text: Consider the following bromides: (A) *tert*-butyl bromide ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$), (B) 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane, (C) 1-bromo-1-methylcyclopentane. The correct order of $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reactivity is:
explanation: $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reactivity follows the stability of the carbocation intermediate formed upon ionization: 1-methylcyclohexyl cation ($\text{B}$) $>$ 1-methylcyclopentyl cation ($\text{C}$) $>$ *tert*-butyl cation ($\text{A}$) (as given in the official answer key).

question_text: Phenol is heated with a solution of mixture of $\text{KBr}$ and $\text{KBrO}_3$. The major product obtained in the above reaction is:
explanation: In acidic medium, $\text{KBr}$ and $\text{KBrO}_3$ generate aqueous bromine ($\text{Br}_2$), which brominates phenol at all *ortho* and *para* positions to yield 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

question_text: Which branched chain isomer of the hydrocarbon with molecular mass $72\text{ u}$ gives only one isomer of mono-substituted alkyl halide?
explanation: A branched alkane with molecular mass $72\text{ u}$ has molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}$ (pentane isomers). Neopentane ($(\text{CH}_3)_4\text{C}$) has all twelve hydrogens chemically equivalent and gives only one monosubstituted haloalkane.

question_text: How many chiral compounds are possible on monochlorination of 2-methylbutane?
explanation: Monochlorination of 2-methylbutane yields four structural monochlorides: 1-chloro-2-methylbutane (chiral), 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (achiral), 2-chloro-3-methylbutane (chiral), and 1-chloro-3-methylbutane (achiral)—giving $2$ chiral constitutional isomers (official key: B).

question_text: Which of the following statements is wrong?
options: Ethyl chloride on reduction with $\text{Zn}-\text{Cu}$ couple and alcohol gives ethane.
The reaction of methyl magnesium bromide with acetone gives butanol-2.
Alkyl halides follow the reactivity sequence $\text{R}-\text{I} > \text{R}-\text{Br} > \text{R}-\text{Cl} > \text{R}-\text{F}$ on reaction with alkenes.
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$ may exist in two isomeric forms.
explanation: Methyl magnesium bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$) reacts with acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) followed by hydrolysis to give *tert*-butyl alcohol (2-methylpropan-2-ol), not butanol-2 (which is obtained from acetaldehyde and $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$). Thus, statement (B) is wrong.

question_text: In the given reaction, $\text{Ph}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+/\text{Hg}^{2+}} \text{A}$, the product 'A' is:
explanation: Acid-catalysed hydration of an unsymmetrical internal alkyne in the presence of $\text{Hg}^{2+}$ forms the enol intermediate, which tautomerises to the ketone (official key: C).

question_text: The major product obtained in the photobromination of 2-methylbutane is:
explanation: Because radical reactivity towards $\text{C}-\text{H}$ cleavage follows $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$ and bromine radicals are highly selective, photobromination of 2-methylbutane occurs predominantly at the tertiary carbon to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

question_text: The product of the reaction between ethylbenzene and *N*-bromosuccinimide (NBS) is:
explanation: *N*-Bromosuccinimide (NBS) provides a low steady-state concentration of $\text{Br}_2$ / $\text{Br}^\bullet$ for selective benzylic/allylic bromination, giving the resonance-stabilised benzylic radical at the $\alpha$-carbon of ethylbenzene and yielding (1-bromoethyl)benzene.

question_text: Allylbenzene ($\text{Ph}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) $+ \text{HCl} \longrightarrow \text{X}$. $\text{X}$ is:
explanation: Protonation of allylbenzene occurs at the terminal alkene carbon to generate the resonance-stabilised secondary benzylic carbocation $\text{Ph}-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$, which then combines with $\text{Cl}^-$ to form $\text{Ph}-\text{CH(Cl)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.

question_text: Aryl fluoride may be prepared from arene diazonium chloride using:
explanation: In the Balz-Schiemann reaction, treating an arenediazonium salt with fluoroboric acid ($\text{HBF}_4$) forms the diazonium fluoroborate, which upon heating ($\Delta$) decomposes to yield the aryl fluoride.

question_text: The Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves condensation of:
options: one molecule of each of aryl-halide and alkyl-halide
one molecule of each of aryl-halide and phenol
explanation: The Wurtz-Fittig reaction is the coupling of one molecule of an aryl halide and one molecule of an alkyl halide using metallic sodium in dry ether to give an alkylarene (e.g., $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + 2\text{Na} + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{ether}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{NaCl}$).

question_text: The order of reactivity of the given haloalkanes towards nucleophile is:
explanation: For a given alkyl group $\text{R}$, the $\text{C}-\text{X}$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases in the order $\text{R}-\text{F} > \text{R}-\text{Cl} > \text{R}-\text{Br} > \text{R}-\text{I}$, so leaving-group ability and reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution increase in the order $\text{RI} > \text{RBr} > \text{RCl} > \text{RF}$.

question_text: In nucleophilic substitution reaction, order of halogens as incoming (attacking) nucleophile is: $\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^-$. The order of halogens as departing nucleophile (leaving group) should be:
explanation: Weaker bases are better leaving groups. Since basicity decreases as $\text{Cl}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{I}^-$, leaving-group ability increases in the order $\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^-$.

question_text: In $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions, the correct order of reactivity for the following compounds: $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCl}$ and $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$ is:
explanation: Steric hindrance at the $\alpha$-carbon increases from $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ ($1^\circ$) to $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCl}$ ($2^\circ$) to $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$ ($3^\circ$), decreasing $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactivity in the order $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCl} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$.

question_text: The correct statement for the molecule $\text{CsI}_3$, is:
explanation: Cesium triiodide ($\text{CsI}_3$) is an ionic compound consisting of the alkali metal cation $\text{Cs}^+$ and the linear triiodide anion $\text{I}_3^-$ (formed from $\text{I}^-$ and $\text{I}_2$).

question_text: In a nucleophilic substitution reaction: $\text{R}-\text{Br} + \text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{DMF}} \text{R}-\text{Cl} + \text{Br}^-$, which one of the following undergoes complete inversion of configuration?
explanation: In a polar aprotic solvent like $\text{DMF}$, $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitution proceeds with inversion of configuration and is favoured for less sterically hindered substrates ($1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$) (official key: D).

question_text: For the compounds $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{F}$, the correct order of increasing $\text{C}$-halogen bond length is:
explanation: As halogen atomic size increases down Group 17 ($\text{F} < \text{Cl} < \text{Br} < \text{I}$), the $\text{C}-\text{X}$ bond length increases steadily: $\text{CH}_3\text{F} < \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} < \text{CH}_3\text{Br} < \text{CH}_3\text{I}$.

question_text: Allyl phenyl ether can be prepared by heating:
explanation: In Williamson ether synthesis, sodium phenoxide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{ONa}$) acts as the nucleophile and attacks allyl bromide ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}$) via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ to form allyl phenyl ether ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$).

question_text: Chlorobenzene reacts with trichloroacetaldehyde (chloral) in the presence of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form DDT as the major product. The structure of DDT is:
explanation: Electrophilic condensation of chloral ($\text{CCl}_3\text{CHO}$) with chlorobenzene in concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ occurs predominantly at the *para* position of two chlorobenzene rings to give 1,1-bis(4-chlorophenyl)-2,2,2-trichloroethane (DDT).

question_text: The major product obtained in the photocataysed bromination of 2-methylbutane is:
explanation: Light-initiated bromination of 2-methylbutane preferentially substitutes the tertiary hydrogen at C-2 because the tertiary alkyl radical is more stable than secondary or primary radicals, yielding 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product.

question_text: Conversion of benzene diazonium chloride to chlorobenzene is an example of which of the following reactions?
explanation: Replacing the diazonium group ($-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$) of an arenediazonium salt with $-\text{Cl}$ or $-\text{Br}$ using $\text{CuCl}/\text{HCl}$ or $\text{CuBr}/\text{HBr}$ is known as the Sandmeyer reaction.

question_text: The major product formed when 1,1,1-trichloropropane is treated with aqueous potassium hydroxide is:
explanation: Hydrolysis of 1,1,1-trichloropropane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CCl}_3$) with aqueous $\text{KOH}$ replaces the three chlorine atoms with $-\text{OH}$ groups to form an unstable *gem*-triol, which spontaneously dehydrates ($-\text{H}_2\text{O}$) to propionic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$).

question_text: The synthesis of alkyl fluorides is best accomplished by:
explanation: Alkyl fluorides are best prepared by the Swarts reaction, which involves heating an alkyl chloride or bromide with a metallic fluoride such as $\text{AgF}$, $\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$, $\text{CoF}_2$, or $\text{SbF}_3$.

question_text: What is the major product expected from the reaction of 1-methylcyclopentene with $\text{DCl}$ (where $\text{D}$ is deuterium)?
explanation: Electrophilic addition of $\text{DCl}$ follows Markovnikov's rule ($\text{Cl}$ adds to the tertiary C-1 bearing $-\text{CH}_3$, and $\text{D}$ adds to C-2) via *anti* addition (official key: A).

question_text:
2-Chloro-2-methylpentane on reaction with sodium methoxide ($\text{NaOCH}_3$) in methanol yields:
(i) $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{C(OCH}_3\text{)(CH}_3)_2$
(ii) $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{C(CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$
(iii) $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH=C(CH}_3)_2$
explanation: A tertiary alkyl halide like 2-chloro-2-methylpentane treated with $\text{NaOCH}_3/\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ undergoes both $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ substitution to give the methyl ether (i) and $\text{E}_1$ elimination to give both the Saytzeff alkene (iii, major) and Hofmann alkene (ii, minor).

question_text: Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol (or cyclohexene derivative) treated sequentially with (1) $\text{NBS}/h\nu$ and (2) $\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ yields:
explanation: Allylic bromination with $\text{NBS}/h\nu$ followed by basic hydrolysis with $\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ replaces bromine with $-\text{OH}$ to give the allylic diol (official key: D).

question_text: Bromination of cyclohexene with $\text{Br}_2 / h\nu$ yields:
explanation: Under photochemical ($h\nu$) conditions, radical allylic substitution at C-3 of cyclohexene (forming the resonance-stabilised allylic radical) predominates over ionic addition across the double bond, yielding 3-bromocyclohexene.

question_text: Which one of the following reagents is not suitable for an elimination reaction on an alkyl halide?
explanation: Elimination reactions require a sufficiently strong base to abstract a $\beta$-proton. Iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) from $\text{NaI}$ is a poor base and a good nucleophile, so it undergoes nucleophilic substitution (Finkelstein exchange) rather than elimination.

question_text: Fluorination of an aromatic ring is easily accomplished by treating a diazonium salt with $\text{HBF}_4$. Which of the following conditions is used to convert the resulting diazonium fluoroborate ($\text{ArN}_2^+\text{BF}_4^-$) into the fluoroarene?
explanation: In the Balz-Schiemann reaction, dry arenediazonium fluoroborate ($\text{ArN}_2^+\text{BF}_4^-$) decomposes upon heating alone ($\Delta$) to give the aryl fluoride along with $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{BF}_3$.

question_text: Which of the following bromo compounds, upon treatment with *tert*-$\text{BuONa}$ followed by addition of bromine water, fails to decolourise the colour of bromine?
options: a bromo compound lacking a $\beta$-hydrogen atom
explanation: Treatment with a base like *tert*-$\text{BuONa}$ forms an alkene only if a $\beta$-hydrogen is present for elimination; the resulting alkene then decolourises bromine water. A substrate lacking a $\beta$-hydrogen cannot undergo $\beta$-elimination to form an alkene and therefore fails to decolourise $\text{Br}_2$ water.

question_text: 3-Methyl-pent-2-ene on reaction with $\text{HBr}$ in presence of peroxide forms an addition product. The number of possible stereoisomers for the product is:
explanation: Peroxide-initiated radical addition of $\text{HBr}$ to 3-methylpent-2-ene gives 3-bromo-3-methylpentane / 2-bromo-3-methylpentane with two stereocentres ($n = 2$), giving $2^n = 2^2 = 4$ possible stereoisomers (official key: C).

question_text:
The increasing order of the reactivity of the following halides for the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction is:
I. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Cl)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$
II. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$
III. $p\text{-H}_3\text{CO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$
explanation: The rate of an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction depends directly on the stability of the intermediate carbocation: primary ($1^\circ$) propyl cation from (II) $<$ secondary ($2^\circ$) *sec*-butyl cation from (I) $<$ resonance- and $+\text{M}$-stabilised *p*-methoxybenzyl cation from (III). Thus, $(\text{II}) < (\text{I}) < (\text{III})$.

question_text: The major product obtained in the reaction of $(+)\text{-1-bromo-1,2-diphenylethane}$ ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH(Br)CH}_2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$) with $t\text{-BuOK} / \Delta$ is:
explanation: Potassium *tert*-butoxide ($t\text{-BuOK}$) is a bulky, strong base that promotes $\text{E}_2$ $\beta$-elimination upon heating ($\Delta$) over substitution, yielding *trans*-stilbene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}=\text{CHC}_6\text{H}_5$) as the major product.

question_text: The major product of the reaction of 2-bromo-2-methyl-1-phenylbutane ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{C(Br)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa} / \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ is:
explanation: With the strong base $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$, $\text{E}_2$ elimination occurs to give the most substituted and phenyl-conjugated alkene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}=\text{C(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, as the major product.

question_text:
The major product of the following reaction is:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Br)CH}_2\text{CH(Br)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{Heat}]{\text{KOH, CH}_3\text{OH}}$
explanation: Heating 2,4-dibromohexane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ ($	ext{KOH}, \text{CH}_3\text{OH}, \Delta$) causes double $\text{E}_2$ dehydrobromination to form the thermodynamically most stable conjugated diene, hexa-2,4-diene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$).

question_text:
In the following reaction sequence:
$\text{I } (\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_2) \xrightarrow{\text{aqueous KOH}} \text{II} \xrightarrow[(ii)\;\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}^+]{(i)\;\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}} \text{III} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous ZnCl}_2 + \text{Conc. HCl}} \text{Gives turbidity immediately}$
Compound $\text{I}$ is:
explanation: Immediate turbidity in the Lucas test indicates that $\text{III}$ is a tertiary alcohol (*tert*-butyl alcohol), formed by reacting a ketone ($\text{II} = \text{acetone}$) with $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$. Acetone is obtained upon aqueous $\text{KOH}$ hydrolysis of the *gem*-dihalide 2,2-dichloropropane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CCl}_2-\text{CH}_3$).

question_text: The major product of the reaction of *trans*-1-bromo-2,2-dimethylcyclohexane with $\text{NaOMe}$ in $\text{MeOH}$ is:
explanation: Because C-2 is quaternary (bearing two methyl groups and no $\beta$-hydrogen) and C-1 is sterically hindered by the adjacent *gem*-dimethyl group, $\text{NaOMe}/\text{MeOH}$ promotes $\text{E}_2$ elimination across C-1 and C-6 to yield 3,3-dimethylcyclohexene as the major product.

question_text: Which of the following bromo-ketones/esters will most readily give the dehydrohalogenation product?
explanation: Dehydrohalogenation proceeds most readily via an $\text{E}_1\text{cb}$ pathway when deprotonation $\alpha$ to the carbonyl group generates a resonance-stabilised enolate carbanion and loss of $\text{Br}^-$ produces a conjugated $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated phenyl-substituted enone ($\text{Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{COCH}_3$) (official key: A).

question_text: The major product of the reaction of $(2R, 5S)\text{-5-bromohex-3-en-2-amine}$ (with wedged $-\text{Br}$ and wedged $-\text{NH}_2$) with $\text{KOH}$ via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ is:
explanation: An $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction with $\text{OH}^-$ occurs exclusively at the stereocentre bearing the leaving group ($-\text{Br}$), inverting its configuration from wedge to dash, while the stereocentre bearing $-\text{NH}_2$ remains untouched (wedged).

question_text: The major product of the reaction of 1-bromo-4-(prop-1-en-1-yl)benzene with $\text{HBr}$ is:
explanation: Electrophilic addition of $\text{HBr}$ across the side-chain double bond proceeds via the more stable resonance-stabilised benzylic carbocation ($p\text{-BrC}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$), yielding 1-bromo-4-(1-bromopropyl)benzene as the major product.

question_text: Major product of the given reaction sequence on *cis*-4-bromo-1-(chloromethyl)cyclohexane (or 2-(2-bromo-5-chlorocyclohexyl)ethanol derivative) treated with: (1) $\text{KOH}$ (aqueous), (2) $\text{CrO}_3 / \text{H}^+$, (3) $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 / \Delta$ is:
explanation: (1) Aqueous $\text{KOH}$ selectively hydrolyses the primary alkyl chloride to a primary alcohol; (2) $\text{CrO}_3/\text{H}^+$ oxidises the primary alcohol to a carboxylic acid; (3) $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4/\Delta$ promotes intramolecular nucleophilic displacement/cyclisation to form a bicyclic lactone (official key: A).

question_text: In the reaction of 1-phenylcyclohexene with (i) $\text{Br}_2$ followed by (ii) $\text{EtOH}$, what will be the major product at the end?
explanation: Step (i) gives *trans*-1,2-dibromo-1-phenylcyclohexane via *anti* bromination. In step (ii), solvolysis in $\text{EtOH}$ ionises the tertiary benzylic $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond to a benzylic carbocation, which is captured by $\text{EtOH}$ preferentially *trans* to the bulky adjacent bromine atom to give *trans*-2-bromo-1-ethoxy-1-phenylcyclohexane.

question_text: The major product of the reaction of 1-(3-chloro-3-methylbutyl)-2-methoxybenzene with (i) $\text{AlCl}_3$ (anhydrous) and (ii) $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is:
explanation: Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ abstracts $\text{Cl}^-$ to generate a stable tertiary carbocation, which undergoes intramolecular Friedel-Crafts alkylation at the less sterically hindered *para* position relative to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group to form the 5-membered indane ring derivative (official key: A).

question_text: The major product obtained in the reaction of 2-((1E,3E)-penta-1,3-dien-1-yl)phenyl acetate with $\text{Br}_2$ ($1\text{ eq.}$) in $\text{MeOH}$ is:
explanation: Electrophilic bromination ($1\text{ eq. } \text{Br}_2$) occurs selectively at the more electron-rich terminal $\text{C}3=\text{C}4$ double bond (since the $\text{C}1=\text{C}2$ bond is conjugated with the aromatic ring) to form a resonance-stabilised allylic/benzylic carbocation intermediate, which is trapped by $\text{MeOH}$ at C-3 to give the bromomethoxy derivative (official key: A).

question_text: The major product of the reaction of 3-(but-3-en-1-yl)phenol with (1) $\text{HCl}$ followed by (2) $\text{AlCl}_3$ (anhydrous) is:
explanation: Step (1) adds $\text{HCl}$ across the terminal alkene via Markovnikov's rule to form 3-(3-chlorobutyl)phenol. Step (2) uses anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to effect intramolecular Friedel-Crafts cyclisation at the less hindered *para* position relative to the $-\text{OH}$ group, yielding 8-methyl-5,6,7,8-tetrahydronaphthalen-2-ol.

question_text:
The major product in the following conversion is:
$p\text{-CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{Heat}]{\text{HBr (excess)}} \text{?}$
explanation: Excess hot $\text{HBr}$ both adds regioselectively across the alkene double bond (forming the benzylic bromide) and cleaves the aryl methyl ether ($\text{Ar}-\text{OCH}_3 + \text{HBr} \longrightarrow \text{Ar}-\text{OH} + \text{CH}_3\text{Br}$), yielding 4-(1-bromopropyl)phenol ($p\text{-HO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$).

question_text: The major product of the reaction of 2-(prop-1-en-2-yl)octahydro-1H-indene with $\text{HCl}$ is:
explanation: Protonation of the exocyclic alkene generates a tertiary carbocation adjacent to the strained 5-membered ring, which undergoes a 1,2-alkyl shift (ring expansion) from a 5-membered ring to a strain-free 6-membered decalin ring, followed by $\text{Cl}^-$ capture to form 3-chloro-2,2-dimethyldecahydronaphthalene.

question_text: The major product of the reaction of 1-chloro-4-(4-isopropylphenyl)butan-2-one with (1) $t\text{-BuOK}$ followed by (2) $\text{Conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4 / \Delta$ is:
explanation: Step (1) causes $\text{E}_2$ elimination of $\text{HCl}$ with $t\text{-BuOK}$ to give the $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone. Step (2) protonates the carbonyl oxygen with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form a resonance-stabilised allylic/hydroxycarbocation, which undergoes intramolecular Friedel-Crafts cyclisation at the less hindered *meta*/*ortho* site to form the 6-membered $\beta$-tetralone derivative (official key: A).

question_text: The major product of the reaction of *o*-chlorotoluene with (1) $\text{Cl}_2 / h\nu$ (2 eq.) followed by (2) $\text{H}_2\text{O}, \Delta$ is:
explanation: Side-chain free-radical chlorination of *o*-chlorotoluene ($	ext{Cl}_2/h\nu$) gives *o*-chlorobenzal chloride ($o\text{-ClC}_6\text{H}_4\text{CHCl}_2$), which upon hydrolysis with water at elevated temperature ($\text{H}_2\text{O}, \Delta$) yields 2-chlorobenzaldehyde ($o\text{-ClC}_6\text{H}_4\text{CHO}$).

question_text: Which of the following potential energy (P.E.) diagrams represents the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction?
options: Two-step profile with a carbocation intermediate valley and the first transition state (T.S. I) higher in energy than the second (T.S. II)
Two-step profile with two transition states of equal energy
Two-step profile with the second transition state (T.S. II) higher in energy than the first (T.S. I)
Single-step concerted profile with one transition state peak
explanation: An $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction is a two-step process proceeding through a carbocation intermediate (a local energy minimum between two transition states), where the first step—heterolytic $\text{C}-\text{X}$ cleavage to form the carbocation—is the rate-determining step and therefore has the highest activation energy barrier ($E_{a1} > E_{a2}$).

question_text:
Increasing order of reactivity of the following compounds for $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ substitution is:
(A) 1-chloro-2-methylpropane ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Cl}$)
(B) chloroethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$)
(C) 1-(chloromethyl)-4-methoxybenzene ($p\text{-CH}_3\text{OC}_6\text{H}_4\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$)
(D) (chloromethyl)benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$)
explanation: $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reactivity follows carbocation stability: ethyl cation ($\text{B}$, $1^\circ$) $<$ isobutyl cation ($\text{A}$, $1^\circ$ with stronger $+\text{I}$ and rapid hydride shift to $3^\circ$) $<$ benzyl cation ($\text{D}$, resonance-stabilised) $<$ *p*-methoxybenzyl cation ($\text{C}$, strongly stabilised by $+\text{M}$ resonance of $-\text{OCH}_3$). Thus, $\text{B} < \text{A} < \text{D} < \text{C}$.

question_text:
The major product of the following reaction is:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)}-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}$
explanation: In a polar protic solvent ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$), solvolysis of 2-bromo-3-methylbutane proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism. The initially formed secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to the more stable tertiary carbocation, which is trapped by $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ to yield 2-methoxy-2-methylbutane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C(OCH}_3\text{)(CH}_3\text{)}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$).

question_text:
Increasing rate of $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction in the following compounds is:
(I) 1-(1-iodoethyl)benzene
(II) 1-(1-iodoethyl)-3-methoxybenzene
(III) 1-(1-iodoethyl)-4-methylbenzene
(IV) 1-(1-iodoethyl)-4-methoxybenzene
explanation: Stability of the intermediate benzylic carbocation increases with electron-donating groups and decreases with electron-withdrawing groups: *meta*-$\text{OCH}_3$ exerts only an electron-withdrawing $-\text{I}$ effect (II, slowest) $<$ unsubstituted phenyl (I) $<$ *para*-$\text{CH}_3$ with $+\text{HC}/+\text{I}$ (III) $<$ *para*-$\text{OCH}_3$ with strong $+\text{M}$ resonance donation (IV, fastest). Thus, $(\text{II}) < (\text{I}) < (\text{III}) < (\text{IV})$.

question_text:
An 'Assertion' and a 'Reason' is given below. Choose the correct answer from the following options:
Assertion (A): Vinyl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution easily.
Reason (R): Even though the intermediate carbocation is stabilized by loosely held $\pi$-electrons, the cleavage is difficult because of the strong bonding.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct statements but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are wrong statements and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is a correct statement but (R) is a wrong statement.
explanation: Vinyl halides ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{X}$) are unreactive towards both $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ and $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitutions (Assertion A is correct). However, Reason R is wrong because a vinylic carbocation ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}^+$) is *not* stabilised by the $\pi$-electrons—the empty $p$ orbital is orthogonal to the $\pi$-bond and resides on an $sp$-hybridised carbon, making it extremely unstable.

question_text:
In the following reaction sequence, structures of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are, respectively:
2-(bromomethyl)-2,3-dihydrobenzofuran $\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}, \Delta} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{Na / Ether}} \text{B}$ (Intramolecular product)
explanation: Treatment of the cyclic ether with $\text{HBr}/\Delta$ cleaves the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ attack of $\text{Br}^-$ to give the dibromophenol intermediate $\text{A}$ (2-(2,3-dibromopropyl)phenol), which upon intramolecular Wurtz-type coupling with $\text{Na}/\text{ether}$ forms the cyclopropane-fused phenol derivative $\text{B}$ (official key: C).

question_text:
Consider the following reactions:
(a) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$
(b) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}_2(\text{excess}) \xrightarrow[\text{dark}]{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{Cl}_6$
(c) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$
(d) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$
Which of these reactions are possible?
explanation: Aryl halides ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ in (a)) and vinyl halides ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$ in (c)) do not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation due to partial double-bond character of the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond. Excess $\text{Cl}_2$ with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ in the dark exhaustively chlorinates benzene to hexachlorobenzene (b), and allyl chloride readily undergoes Friedel-Crafts allylation to give allylbenzene (d). Thus, (b) and (d) are possible.

question_text: For the reactions of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ with nucleophile/base $\text{Z}^-$ giving substitution ($k_s$) and elimination ($k_e$), where $\text{Z}^- = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-\text{ (A)}$ or $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CO}^-\text{ (B)}$, and $\mu = \frac{k_s}{k_e}$, the correct option is:
explanation: Potassium *tert*-butoxide (B) is much bulkier and more strongly basic than ethoxide (A), so it strongly favours $\text{E}_2$ elimination over $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitution: $k_e(B) > k_e(A)$ and $k_s(A) > k_s(B)$. Consequently, the substitution-to-elimination ratio satisfies $\mu_A > \mu_B$.

question_text:
The decreasing order of reactivity towards dehydrohalogenation ($\text{E}_1$) reaction of the following compounds is:
(A) 1-chloropentane
(B) 2-chloropentane
(C) 2-chloro-3-methylbutane
(D) 3-chloro-3-methylpentane
explanation: $\text{E}_1$ dehydrohalogenation proceeds via carbocation formation in the rate-determining step, so reactivity increases with carbocation stability ($3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$) (official key: A, $\text{D} > \text{B} > \text{C} > \text{A}$).

question_text: Which of these will produce the highest yield in a Friedel-Crafts reaction?
explanation: Aniline and benzamide coordinate strongly with the Lewis acid catalyst ($\text{AlCl}_3$) to form deactivating complexes, and chlorobenzene is deactivated by $-\text{I}$. Phenol has a strong $+\text{M}$ activating $-\text{OH}$ group and gives the highest yield among the given choices.

question_text: Which of the following compounds will show retention in configuration on nucleophilic substitution by $\text{OH}^-$ ion?
explanation: In $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(C}_2\text{H}_5\text{)}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$, the nucleophilic substitution takes place at the achiral $-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ carbon without breaking any bond to the adjacent chiral carbon ($\text{C}-2$), so the configuration at the stereocentre is completely retained.

question_text:
Consider the reaction sequence given below:
(1) $t\text{-BuBr} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} t\text{-BuOH} + \text{HBr}$, $\text{rate} = k[t\text{-BuBr}]$
(2) $t\text{-BuBr} \xrightarrow{\text{OH}^- / \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Br}^-$, $\text{rate} = k[t\text{-BuBr}][\text{OH}^-]$
Which of the following statements is true?
options: Changing the base from $\text{OH}^-$ to $\text{OR}^-$ will have no effect on reaction (2)
Changing the concentration of base will have no effect on reaction (1)
Doubling the concentration of base will double the rate of both the reactions
Changing the concentration of base will have no effect on reaction (2)
explanation: Reaction (1) follows first-order $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ kinetics ($\text{rate} = k[t\text{-BuBr}]$), which is independent of the base/nucleophile concentration. Reaction (2) follows second-order $\text{E}_2$ kinetics ($\text{rate} = k[t\text{-BuBr}][\text{OH}^-]$), which depends on both substrate and base concentrations.

question_text: The major product obtained from $\text{E}_2$-elimination of 3-bromo-2-fluoropentane is:
explanation: Because $-\text{Br}$ is a far better leaving group than $-\text{F}$ and the strong inductive ($-\text{I}$) effect of fluorine makes the $\beta$-hydrogen at C-2 more acidic than the $\beta$-hydrogens at C-4, $\text{E}_2$ elimination removes $\text{H}$ from C-2 and $\text{Br}$ from C-3 to form 2-fluoropent-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{C(F)CH}_3$).

question_text:
The mechanism of $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction is given as:
$\text{R}-\text{X} \longrightarrow \text{R}^+\text{X}^- \text{ (Ion pair)} \longrightarrow \text{R}^+ \| \text{X}^- \text{ (Solvent separated ion pair)} \xrightarrow{\text{Y}^-} \text{R}-\text{Y} + \text{X}^-$
A student writes general characteristics based on the given mechanism as:
(a) The reaction is favoured by weak nucleophiles.
(b) $\text{R}^+$ would be easily formed if the substituents are bulky.
(c) The reaction is accompanied by racemization.
(d) The reaction is favoured by non-polar solvents.
Which observations are correct?
explanation: In an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction, the rate-determining ionization does not require a strong nucleophile (a is correct), bulky alkyl groups stabilise the carbocation via hyperconjugation/inductive effects and relieve steric crowding upon ionization (b is correct), planar carbocation attack from both faces leads to racemization (c is correct), and polar protic solvents—not non-polar solvents—favour ionization (d is incorrect).

question_text: The major product in the reaction of 2-(bromomethyl)-1,1-dimethylcyclopentane (or 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylcyclohexane) with $t\text{-BuOH} / \text{Heat}$ is:
explanation: Under solvolytic $\text{E}_1$ heating conditions in $t\text{-BuOH}$, ionization forms a secondary carbocation that undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to a more stable tertiary carbocation, followed by loss of a proton to give the tetrasubstituted Saytzeff alkene, 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene.

question_text:
The decreasing order of reactivity of the following compounds towards nucleophilic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}2$) is:
(I) 4-nitrobenzyl chloride
(II) 2,4-dinitrobenzyl chloride
(III) 3,5-dinitrobenzyl chloride
(IV) 4-methoxybenzyl chloride (or benzyl chloride)
explanation: Electron-withdrawing $-\text{NO}_2$ groups increase the electrophilicity of the benzylic carbon and stabilise the negatively charged $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ transition state: 2,4-dinitro (II, two $-\text{I}/-\text{M}$ groups) $>$ 3,5-dinitro (III, two $-\text{I}$ groups) $>$ 4-nitro (IV) $>$ unsubstituted/electron-rich (I) (official key: B).

question_text:
The major product '$\text{Y}$' in the following reaction is:
2-chloro-3-methylbutane $\xrightarrow[\text{Heat}]{\text{EtONa}} \text{X} \xrightarrow{\text{HBr}} \text{Y}$
explanation: In the first step, strong base $\text{EtONa}$ induces $\text{E}_2$ elimination of 2-chloro-3-methylbutane to yield the Saytzeff alkene 2-methylbut-2-ene ($\text{X}$). In the second step, $\text{HBr}$ adds across 2-methylbut-2-ene via Markovnikov's rule (through a tertiary carbocation) to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane ($\text{Y}$).

question_text:
The increasing order of the boiling points of the major products $\text{A}$, $\text{B}$ and $\text{C}$ of the following reactions will be:
(a) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2} \text{A}$
(b) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \longrightarrow \text{B}$
(c) $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \longrightarrow \text{C}$
explanation: $\text{A}$ is 1-bromobutane (straight-chain $1^\circ$ halide), $\text{B}$ is 2-bromobutane ($2^\circ$ halide), and $\text{C}$ is 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (compact spherical $3^\circ$ halide). Among isomeric bromobutanes ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Br}$), surface area and London dispersion forces decrease with increased branching, so boiling points follow $\text{C} < \text{B} < \text{A}$.

question_text: What is the major product formed by $\text{HI}$ on reaction with 3-methylbut-1-ene ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$)?
explanation: Electrophilic addition of $\text{HI}$ to 3-methylbut-1-ene initially generates the secondary carbocation $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}_3$, which undergoes a rapid 1,2-hydride shift to form the more stable tertiary carbocation $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}^+-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, followed by $\text{I}^-$ attack to give 2-iodo-2-methylbutane.

question_text: The product formed in the first step of the reaction of $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_3$ (2,4-dibromohexane) with excess $\text{Mg}/\text{Et}_2\text{O}$ ($\text{Et} = \text{C}_2\text{H}_5$) is:
explanation: In a 1,3-dihaloalkane such as 2,4-dibromohexane, reaction with excess magnesium in dry diethyl ether ($\text{Mg}/\text{Et}_2\text{O}$) converts both $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bonds into the bis-Grignard reagent 2,4-bis(bromomagnesio)hexane.

question_text:
For the given reaction:
4-ethylbenzonitrile $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2, \text{UV light}} \text{'A'}$ (major monobrominated product)
What is $\text{A}$?
explanation: Under UV light, free-radical bromination occurs selectively at the benzylic $\text{C}-\text{H}$ position because the resulting benzylic radical is strongly stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring, yielding 4-(1-bromoethyl)benzonitrile.

question_text:
For the given reaction:
1-bromoprop-1-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CHBr}$) $\xrightarrow[2.\;\text{Red hot iron tube, } 873\text{ K}]{1.\;\text{NaNH}_2} \text{A}$ (major product)
What is $\text{A}$?
explanation: Step 1 dehydrobrominates 1-bromoprop-1-ene with $\text{NaNH}_2$ to form propyne ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$). Step 2 carries out cyclic trimerisation of three molecules of propyne over a red-hot iron tube at $873\text{ K}$ to yield 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (mesitylene).

question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I:
(a) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{N}_2$
(b) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}, \text{HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{N}_2$
(c) $2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{Ether}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 + 2\text{NaCl}$
(d) $2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{Ether}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5 + 2\text{NaCl}$
List-II: (i) Wurtz reaction, (ii) Sandmeyer reaction, (iii) Fittig reaction, (iv) Gatterman reaction
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
Identify the reagent(s) '$\text{A}$' and condition(s) for the conversion of cyclohexene to 3-chlorocyclohexene:
explanation: Allylic chlorination of cyclohexene at the C-3 position proceeds via a free-radical chain mechanism initiated by $\text{Cl}_2$ in the presence of UV light ($h\nu$).

question_text: Reaction of Grignard reagent, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$ with $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}$ followed by hydrolysis gives compound $\text{A}$, which reacts instantly with Lucas reagent to give compound $\text{B}$ ($\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{13}\text{Cl}$). The compound $\text{B}$ is:
explanation: Immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent ($	ext{conc. HCl} + \text{anhyd. ZnCl}_2$) proves $\text{A}$ is a tertiary alcohol, meaning $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}$ is acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$). Addition of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$ gives 2-phenylbutan-2-ol ($\text{A}$), which reacts with Lucas reagent to form 2-chloro-2-phenylbutane ($\text{B}$).

question_text:
$\text{BrCH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow[\text{dry HCl gas}]{\text{EtOH (excess)}} \text{A (major product)} \xrightarrow{t\text{-BuO}^-\text{K}^+} \text{B (major product)}$
[Where $\text{Et} = -\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$, $t\text{-Bu} = (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-$]
Consider the above reaction sequence. Product '$\text{A}$' and Product '$\text{B}$' formed respectively are:
explanation: In the first step, excess $\text{EtOH}$ with dry $\text{HCl}$ gas protects the aldehyde group of bromoacetaldehyde as the diethyl acetal $\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH(OEt)}_2$ ($\text{A}$). In the second step, bulky base $t\text{-BuO}^-\text{K}^+$ performs $\text{E}_2$ dehydrobromination to yield ketene diethyl acetal $\text{CH}_2=\text{C(OEt)}_2$ ($\text{B}$).

question_text:
What is $\text{A}$ in the following reaction?
Potassium phthalimide $+ \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow[(ii)\;\text{OH}^-/\text{H}_2\text{O}]{(i)\;\Delta} \text{A}$ (Major Product)
explanation: This is the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis: potassium phthalimide reacts with benzyl bromide via $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ to form $N$-benzylphthalimide, which upon alkaline hydrolysis ($\text{OH}^-/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) gives primary amine benzylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$) along with phthalate salt.

question_text:
The correct options for the products $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ of the following reactions on phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) are:
$\text{A} \xleftarrow{\text{Br}_2\text{ (Excess)},\; \text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2,\; \text{CS}_2,\; <5^\circ\text{C}} \text{B}$
explanation: In polar aqueous medium ($	ext{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$), phenol ionises to the strongly activating phenoxide ion, undergoing trisubstitution to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol ($\text{A}$). In a low-polarity solvent like $\text{CS}_2$ at low temperature ($<5^\circ\text{C}$), monobromination occurs to give *para*-bromophenol ($\text{B}$) as the major product.

question_text:
Among the following compounds $\text{I} - \text{IV}$, which one forms a yellow precipitate on reacting sequentially with (i) $\text{NaOH}$ (ii) dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ (iii) $\text{AgNO}_3$?
I. 1-chlorocyclohexene
II. 1-bromocyclohexene
III. 1-iodocyclohexene
IV. 3-(iodomethyl)cyclohexene (or (iodomethyl)benzene)
explanation: Vinylic halides (I, II, III) do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ due to partial double-bond character of the $\text{C}(sp^2)-\text{X}$ bond. Only the allylic/benzylic primary iodide in $\text{IV}$ undergoes substitution to release $\text{I}^-$ ions, which form a yellow precipitate of $\text{AgI}$ with $\text{AgNO}_3$.

question_text:
In the following sequence of reactions, the major product $\text{P}$ is:
Chlorocyclopentane $+ \text{Mg} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} [\text{A}] \xrightarrow{\text{ethanol}} \text{P}$ (Major Product)
explanation: Chlorocyclopentane reacts with $\text{Mg}$ in dry ether to form cyclopentylmagnesium chloride ($[\text{A}]$). Because Grignard reagents are strong bases, reaction with ethanol (which has an acidic $-\text{OH}$ proton) protonates the carbanion to form cyclopentane ($\text{P}$).

question_text:
The correct order of reactivity of the given chlorides with acetate in acetic acid is:
(I) 1-chloro-3-methylbut-2-ene
(II) 1-chloro-3-methylbutane
(III) 3-chloro-3-methylbut-1-ene
explanation: Acetolysis in acetic acid proceeds via an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism, where reactivity correlates with carbocation stability and ease of ionization (official key: C).

question_text:
The structure of product $\text{C}$, formed by the following sequence of reactions is:
$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{SOCl}_2 \longrightarrow \text{A} \xrightarrow[\text{AlCl}_3]{\text{Benzene}} \text{B} \xrightarrow[-\text{OH}]{\text{KCN}} \text{C}$
explanation: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{SOCl}_2 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ ($\text{A}$); Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene gives acetophenone, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ ($\text{B}$); nucleophilic addition of $\text{CN}^-$ from $\text{KCN}/\text{OH}^-$ to the carbonyl group gives acetophenone cyanohydrin, 2-hydroxy-2-phenylpropanenitrile ($\text{C}$).

question_text:
The major product of the following reaction is:
4-chloro-5-methylcyclopent-1-ene $\xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}, \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}}$ Major Product
explanation: Alcoholic $\text{NaOH}$ ($\text{NaOH}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) promotes $\text{E}_2$ dehydrohalogenation to form the more stable conjugated Saytzeff diene, 1-methylcyclopenta-1,3-diene (official key: B; note: NTA key listed D).

question_text:
1-(bromomethyl)-4-methoxybenzene $\xrightarrow[(iv)\;\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}]{(i)\;\text{NaCN},\; (ii)\;\text{OH}^-,\; (iii)\;\text{cyclohexanone}}$ Product
The major product of the above reactions is:
explanation: (i) $\text{NaCN}$ performs $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitution to form 2-(4-methoxyphenyl)acetonitrile; (ii) $\text{OH}^-$ deprotonates the acidic benzylic $\alpha$-carbon to form a resonance-stabilised carbanion; (iii) nucleophilic addition to cyclohexanone gives a $\beta$-hydroxynitrile; (iv) catalytic hydrogenation ($\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$) reduces the $-\text{CN}$ group to $-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, yielding 1-(2-amino-1-(4-methoxyphenyl)ethyl)cyclohexan-1-ol.

question_text:
3-chlorocyclohex-1-ene $\xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{P}$ (Major Product)
Consider the above reaction. The number of $\pi$-electrons present in the product '$\text{P}$' is ______.
explanation: Aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ ($\text{NaOH}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) carries out nucleophilic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}2$) on 3-chlorocyclohex-1-ene to yield cyclohex-2-en-1-ol ($\text{P}$), which retains one $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond containing $2$ $\pi$-electrons.

question_text:
The major product ($\text{P}$) in the reaction:
4-phenylbut-1-ene ($\text{Ph}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) $\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}} \text{? } (\text{P})$ [$\text{Ph}$ is $-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$] is:
explanation: Electrophilic addition of $\text{HBr}$ across the alkene double bond follows Markovnikov's rule (with benzylic bromination/substitution as shown in the diagram), giving 1,3-dibromo-1-phenylbutane (official key: B).

question_text:
The major product in the reaction:
$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{Cl} + \text{K}^+\text{O}^--\text{C(CH}_3)_3 \longrightarrow \text{?}$ is:
explanation: Potassium *tert*-butoxide ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CO}^-\text{K}^+$) is a sterically bulky strong base that exclusively causes $\text{E}_2$ $\beta$-elimination on *tert*-butyl chloride ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$) to form 2-methylprop-1-ene (isobutylene).

question_text:
In the given reaction:
$2\text{A} \xrightarrow[(iii)\;\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}^+]{(i)\;2\text{Mg},\; \text{THF};\; (ii)\;\text{Methyl benzoate}} \text{Triphenylmethanol } (\text{Ph}_3\text{COH})$
'$\text{A}$' can be:
explanation: Bromobenzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Br}$) reacts with $\text{Mg}$ in $\text{THF}$ to form phenylmagnesium bromide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$). Two equivalents of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$ react with methyl benzoate ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOCH}_3$) followed by acidic hydrolysis to yield triphenylmethanol ($\text{Ph}_3\text{COH}$).

question_text:
The major product of the following reaction is:
$(R)\text{-1-(1-bromoethyl)-4-fluoro-2-nitrobenzene} \xrightarrow{\text{PhS}^-\text{Na}^+,\; \text{DMF}}$
explanation: In a polar aprotic solvent ($\text{DMF}$), the strong, soft nucleophile $\text{PhS}^-$ selectively displaces the benzylic $-\text{Br}$ leaving group via a concerted $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction with inversion of configuration at the benzylic stereocentre, while the aryl $\text{C}-\text{F}$ bond remains intact.

question_text: Which one of the following compounds is inactive towards $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction?
explanation: In 1-chlorobicyclo[2.2.2]octane, the chlorine atom is at a rigid bridgehead carbon that cannot flatten into the planar $sp^2$ geometry required for a carbocation (Bredt's rule), making it virtually inert towards $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ ionization.

question_text:
Consider the following reaction:
$\text{A} \xrightarrow[3.\;\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}^+/\Delta]{1.\;\text{Cl}_2/h\nu,\; 2.\;\text{CN}^-} \text{4-bromophenylacetic acid}$
What is $\text{A}$ in the above reaction?
explanation: 4-Bromotoluene ($\text{A}$) undergoes benzylic free-radical monochlorination ($\text{Cl}_2/h\nu$) to give 4-bromobenzyl chloride, which reacts with $\text{CN}^-$ to give 4-bromobenzyl cyanide and hydrolyses under acidic heating ($\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}^+/\Delta$) to 4-bromophenylacetic acid.

question_text:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3} \text{'A' (Major Product)}$
The stable carbocation formed in the above reaction is:
explanation: In Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with 1-chloropropane and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$, the incipient primary *n*-propyl carbocation rearranges via a 1,2-hydride shift to the more stable secondary isopropyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^+\text{H}-\text{CH}_3$), yielding cumene as the major product.

question_text: Most stable product of the reaction of $(1R, 2R)\text{-2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol}$ (wedged $-\text{OH}$, dashed $-\text{CH}_3$) with (i) $\text{TsCl}$ (or $\text{SOCl}_2$), Pyridine followed by (ii) $\text{NaCN}, \text{DMF}$ is:
explanation: Conversion of the alcohol into a good leaving group (tosylate/chloride in pyridine) retains configuration at C-1, and subsequent $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ displacement by $\text{CN}^-$ in $\text{DMF}$ proceeds with Walden inversion at C-1 (converting wedged $-\text{OH}$ into dashed $-\text{CN}$), while C-2 remains unchanged (official key: B).

question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Experimental reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ with aniline and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ does not give *o*- and *p*-methylaniline.
Reason (R): The $-\text{NH}_2$ group of aniline becomes deactivating because of salt formation with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ and hence yields *m*-methylaniline as the product.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Aniline (a Lewis base) reacts with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ (a Lewis acid) to form an insoluble salt/complex ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2^+\text{AlCl}_3^-$) that strongly deactivates the ring so that *no* Friedel-Crafts reaction occurs at all—it does not yield *m*-methylaniline. Hence, (A) is true, but (R) is false.

question_text: Total number of isomers (including stereoisomers) obtained on monochlorination of methylcyclohexane is ______.
explanation:
Monochlorination of methylcyclohexane yields five structural isomers:
1. (Chloromethyl)cyclohexane ($1$ achiral isomer)
2. 1-Chloro-1-methylcyclohexane ($1$ achiral isomer)
3. 1-Chloro-2-methylcyclohexane ($2$ chiral centres $\to 4$ stereoisomers)
4. 1-Chloro-3-methylcyclohexane ($2$ chiral centres $\to 4$ stereoisomers)
5. 1-Chloro-4-methylcyclohexane ($2$ *cis*/*trans* geometrical isomers)
Total $= 1 + 1 + 4 + 4 + 2 = 12$ isomers.

question_text:
The structure of $\text{A}$ in the given reaction is:
$\text{R}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}} \text{A (major product)}$
explanation: In the presence of base ($\text{NaOH}$), an $\alpha$-proton is abstracted from the methyl ketone to generate an enolate carbanion ($\text{R}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2^-$), which undergoes $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ alkylation with ethyl bromide ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}$) to yield the chain-extended ketone $\text{R}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (official key: C).

question_text:
$\text{'A'} \xleftarrow[\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}, \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{AgCN}} \text{Cyclohexyl chloride} \xrightarrow[\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}, \text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{NaCN}} \text{'B'}$
Considering the above reactions, the functional groups attached to the cyclohexane ring in compound '$\text{A}$' and compound '$\text{B}$' respectively are:
explanation: Cyanide is an ambident nucleophile. Covalent $\text{AgCN}$ has the $\text{Ag}-\text{C}$ bond blocked, so attack occurs through nitrogen to give the isocyanide ($-\text{N}^+\equiv\text{C}^-$, compound $\text{A}$). Ionic $\text{NaCN}$ provides free $\text{CN}^-$ ions that attack predominantly through carbon to form the stronger $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond, yielding the cyanide/nitrile ($-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$, compound $\text{B}$).

question_text:
Compound '$\text{A}$' (2-bromo-3-methylbutane) undergoes the following sequence of reactions to give compound '$\text{B}$':
$\text{Compound 'A'} \xrightarrow[(ii)\;\text{D}_2\text{O}]{(i)\;\text{Mg},\; \text{Et}_2\text{O}} \text{B}$ [where $\text{Et}$ is $-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$]
The correct structure and chirality of compound '$\text{B}$' is:
explanation: 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane reacts with $\text{Mg}$ in dry ether to form the Grignard reagent, which upon reaction with $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ yields 2-deuterio-3-methylbutane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CHD}-\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$). Because $\text{C}-2$ is bonded to four different groups ($-\text{H}$, $-\text{D}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$), compound '$\text{B}$' is chiral.

question_text: Number of moles of $\text{AgCl}$ formed when $1\text{ mol}$ of 1,2,3-trichloro-3-methylcyclohex-1-ene reacts with excess $\text{AgNO}_3$ is ______.
explanation: Vinylic chlorines at $\text{C}-1$ and $\text{C}-2$ are attached to $sp^2$ double-bonded carbons and do not ionise with $\text{AgNO}_3$. The remaining two chlorines at allylic/tertiary positions ionise readily to form stable allylic/tertiary carbocations, precipitating $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ (official key: 2).

question_text:
In the following given reaction, '$\text{A}$' is:
(prop-1-en-2-yl)cyclobutane $+ \text{HBr} \longrightarrow \text{'A' (major product)}$
explanation: Protonation of the alkene forms a tertiary carbocation adjacent to the strained 4-membered cyclobutane ring. Ring expansion relieves angle strain to give a 5-membered cyclopentyl carbocation, which undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to a more stable tertiary cyclopentyl carbocation and reacts with $\text{Br}^-$ to give 1-bromo-1,2-dimethylcyclopentane (official key: C).

question_text:
Assertion A: Hydrolysis of an alkyl chloride is a slow reaction but in the presence of $\text{NaI}$, the rate of hydrolysis increases.
Reason R: $\text{I}^-$ is a good nucleophile as well as a good leaving group.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
explanation: $\text{NaI}$ catalyses the hydrolysis of alkyl chlorides via nucleophilic catalysis: $\text{I}^-$ (a strong nucleophile) displaces $\text{Cl}^-$ to form $\text{R}-\text{I}$, and because $\text{I}^-$ is also a much better leaving group than $\text{Cl}^-$, $\text{R}-\text{I}$ is rapidly hydrolysed by water to $\text{R}-\text{OH}$. Thus, both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

question_text: Maximum number of isomeric monochloro derivatives which can be obtained from 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane by chlorination is ______.
explanation: 2,2,5,5-Tetramethylhexane ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C(CH}_3)_3$) has only two sets of chemically equivalent hydrogens: the $18$ primary methyl hydrogens and the $4$ secondary methylene hydrogens. Chlorination at a methyl group gives 1-chloro-2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane ($1$ achiral isomer), while chlorination at a $-\text{CH}_2-$ group gives 3-chloro-2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane, which has a chiral carbon and exists as a pair of enantiomers ($2$ stereoisomers). Total isomers $= 1 + 2 = 3$.

question_text:
Identify the correct order for the given property for following compounds:
(A) Boiling Point: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$
(B) Density: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{I}$
(C) Boiling Point: $\text{CH}_3\text{Br} < \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 < \text{CHBr}_3$
(D) Density: $\text{CHBr}_3 < \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 < \text{CH}_3\text{Br}$
(E) Boiling Point: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Cl} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Boiling points increase with molecular mass and chain length (A and C are correct) and decrease with branching among isomers (E is correct). Density increases with atomic mass and number of halogen atoms ($\text{RCl} < \text{RBr} < \text{RI}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{Br} < \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 < \text{CHBr}_3$), so B and D are incorrect. Thus, (A), (C) and (E) only.

question_text: The one giving maximum number of isomeric alkenes on dehydrohalogenation reaction is (excluding rearrangement):
explanation: 2-Bromopentane has two non-equivalent sets of $\beta$-hydrogens (at C-1 and C-3), yielding $3$ isomeric alkenes upon dehydrohalogenation: pent-1-ene, *cis*-pent-2-ene, and *trans*-pent-2-ene (whereas the other three bromides each have only one type of $\beta$-hydrogen and give only $1$ alkene).

question_text: In the conversion of 4-nitrotoluene ($\text{X}$) to 3,5-dibromotoluene ($\text{Y}$), the sequence of reagents to be used will be:
explanation: (i) $\text{Fe}/\text{H}^+$ reduces $-\text{NO}_2$ to $-\text{NH}_2$ (giving *p*-toluidine); (ii) $\text{Br}_2(\text{aq})$ brominates both positions *ortho* to $-\text{NH}_2$ (giving 2,6-dibromo-4-methylaniline); (iii) $\text{HNO}_2$ converts $-\text{NH}_2$ to $-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$; (iv) $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ reduces the diazonium group to $-\text{H}$, yielding 3,5-dibromotoluene ($\text{Y}$).

question_text: The correct order of melting point of dichlorobenzenes is:
explanation: Due to its high molecular symmetry, *para*-dichlorobenzene ($323\text{ K}$) packs much more efficiently into a crystal lattice than *ortho*-dichlorobenzene ($256\text{ K}$) or *meta*-dichlorobenzene ($249\text{ K}$), giving the melting point order *p*-dichlorobenzene $>$ *o*-dichlorobenzene $>$ *m*-dichlorobenzene.

question_text: In the following halogenated organic compounds, the one with maximum number of chlorine atoms in its structure is:

Identify the incorrect option from the following:

(D) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[(ii)\;\text{HCl}]{(i)\;\text{NaOH},\; 623\text{ K},\; 300\text{ atm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$

question_text: For the reaction: $\text{RCH}_2\text{Br} + \text{I}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Acetone}} \text{RCH}_2\text{I}_{\text{major}} + \text{Br}^-$, the correct statement is:

The solvent used in the reaction solvates the ions formed in rate determining step.
explanation: In this Finkelstein $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction in polar aprotic acetone, the negative charge in the transition state ($[\text{I}^{\delta-}\cdots\text{CH}_2(\text{R})\cdots\text{Br}^{\delta-}]$) is dispersed over both incoming and leaving halogens, making the transition state less polar (more charge-delocalised) than the localised $\text{I}^-$ reactant anion.

question_text:
Choose the halogen which is most reactive towards $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction in the given compounds (A, B, C & D):
A: 1-bromo-4-(2-bromoethyl)benzene [$\text{Br}_{(a)}$ benzylic/primary vs $\text{Br}_{(b)}$ aryl]
B: 1-iodo-4-(iodomethyl)cyclohex-1-ene [$\text{I}_{(a)}$ allylic vs $\text{I}_{(b)}$ vinylic]
C: 1,4-dibromobicyclo[2.2.2]octane derivative [$\text{Br}_{(a)}$ bridgehead vs $\text{Br}_{(b)}$ non-bridgehead]
D: 1,3-dibromo-3-methylbutane [$\text{Br}_{(a)}$ tertiary vs $\text{Br}_{(b)}$ primary]
explanation: Reactivity in $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ is governed by carbocation stability: in A, benzylic $\text{Br}_{(a)}$ ionises far more readily than aryl $\text{Br}_{(b)}$; in B, allylic $\text{I}_{(a)}$ ionises far more readily than vinylic $\text{I}_{(b)}$; in C, non-bridgehead $\text{Br}_{(b)}$ ionises rather than strained bridgehead $\text{Br}_{(a)}$; in D, tertiary $\text{Br}_{(a)}$ forms a stable $3^\circ$ carbocation faster than primary $\text{Br}_{(b)}$.

question_text:
The correct order of reactivity of following haloarenes towards nucleophilic substitution with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ is:
(A) chlorobenzene
(B) 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene
(C) 1-chloro-4-methoxybenzene
(D) 1-chloro-2,4,6-trinitrobenzene
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$) proceeds via a negatively charged Meisenheimer carbanion intermediate, which is strongly stabilised by electron-withdrawing $-\text{NO}_2$ groups at *ortho*/*para* positions and destabilised by electron-donating $+\text{M}$ $-\text{OCH}_3$ groups: $\text{D} > \text{B} > \text{A} > \text{C}$.

question_text:

(A) $\text{S}_\text{N}2$: 2-bromobutane $>$ 2-bromo-2-methylbutane

Friedel-Crafts acylation *meta* to $-\text{NO}_2$ on the nitro-substituted ring
explanation: In a biaryl/diarylmethane system containing an electron-rich ring (activated by $+\text{M}$ $-\text{OCH}_3$ and $+\text{HC}$ $-\text{CH}_3$) and a strongly deactivated nitrobenzene ring ($-\text{M}/-\text{I}$ $-\text{NO}_2$), Friedel-Crafts acylation occurs exclusively on the activated methoxy-substituted ring *ortho* to the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group (official key: A).

question_text: 2-Methylpropyl bromide reacts with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$ and gives '$\text{A}$' whereas on reaction with $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ it gives '$\text{B}$'. The mechanism followed in these reactions and the products '$\text{A}$' and '$\text{B}$' respectively are:
explanation: With the strong nucleophile $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$, primary isobutyl bromide undergoes concerted $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitution without rearrangement to give isobutyl ethyl ether ($\text{A}$). With the weak nucleophile $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ (solvolysis), $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ ionization accompanied by a 1,2-hydride shift forms the stable *tert*-butyl carbocation, yielding *tert*-butyl ethyl ether ($\text{B}$).

The major product formed in the Friedel-Crafts acylation of chlorobenzene with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is:
explanation: Chlorine is an *ortho*/*para*-directing group in electrophilic aromatic substitution. Because of steric hindrance at the *ortho* position, Friedel-Crafts acylation of chlorobenzene with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}/\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3$ yields the *para*-isomer, 4-chloroacetophenone, as the major product.

question_text: The correct statement regarding nucleophilic substitution reaction in a chiral alkyl halide is:
options: Retention occurs in $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction and inversion occurs in $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction.
Racemisation occurs in $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction and retention occurs in $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction.
Racemisation occurs in both $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ and $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions.
Racemisation occurs in $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction and inversion occurs in $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction.
explanation: In an $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction, the planar $sp^2$ carbocation intermediate is attacked equally from both faces, leading to racemisation. In an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction, concerted backside attack by the nucleophile causes complete Walden inversion of configuration.

question_text: Which among the following halides will not show $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction?
explanation: 1-Chloroprop-1-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{Cl}$) is a vinylic halide whose $\text{C}(sp^2)-\text{Cl}$ bond has partial double-bond character and whose heterolytic cleavage would generate an extremely unstable vinylic carbocation ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{C}^+\text{H}$), so it does not undergo $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reaction.

question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:
Assertion A: Aryl halides cannot be prepared by replacement of hydroxyl group of phenol by halogen atom.
Reason R: Phenols react with halogen acids violently.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
explanation: In phenol, lone-pair delocalisation into the benzene ring imparts partial double-bond character to the $\text{C}(sp^2)-\text{OH}$ bond, making it too strong to be cleaved by halogen acids ($\text{HX}$) to give aryl halides (Assertion A is true, whereas Reason R is false because phenols do not react violently with $\text{HX}$).

question_text: Alkyl halide is converted into alkyl isocyanide by reaction with:
explanation: Silver cyanide ($\text{AgCN}$) is predominantly covalent, leaving only the lone pair on the nitrogen atom free to attack the alkyl halide, yielding alkyl isocyanide ($\text{R}-\text{NC}$) as the major product.

Given below are two statements:

Statement II: A secondary alkyl halide when treated with a large excess of ethanol follows $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism.

options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

explanation: Secondary alkyl halides are borderline substrates: in the presence of a high concentration of a strong, unhindered nucleophile, the bimolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ pathway dominates (Statement I is true), whereas in a large excess of a polar protic weak nucleophile like ethanol (solvolysis), the unimolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ pathway dominates (Statement II is true).

explanation: Toluene ($\text{B}$) is activated by hyperconjugation and $+\text{I}$ of $-\text{CH}_3$; benzene ($\text{A}$) is the reference; chlorobenzene ($\text{C}$) is weakly deactivated by $-\text{I}$ of $-\text{Cl}$; nitrobenzene ($\text{D}$) is strongly deactivated by $-\text{M}$ and $-\text{I}$ of $-\text{NO}_2$. question_text: Which among the following compounds will undergo fastest $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction?
explanation: $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactivity depends inversely on steric hindrance around the reactive carbon: unhindered primary alkyl halide ($1^\circ$) reacts fastest compared to secondary ($2^\circ$), neopentyl ($\beta$-branched $1^\circ$), and tertiary ($3^\circ$) halides.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions are 'stereospecific', indicating that they result in the formation of only one stereoisomer as the product.
Statement (II): $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reactions generally result in formation of product as racemic mixtures.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
explanation: $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions proceed with $100\%$ stereospecific Walden inversion at the chiral centre to give a single inverted stereoisomer (Statement I is true), whereas $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ reactions proceed through a planar $sp^2$ carbocation intermediate attacked equally from both faces to give a racemic mixture (Statement II is true).

explanation: 2-Bromobutane reacts with $\text{Mg}/\text{Et}_2\text{O}$ to form *sec*-butylmagnesium bromide, which reacts with $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ to give 2-deuteriobutane ($\text{B}$). Heating 2-bromobutane with $\text{CoF}_2$ (Swarts reaction) exchanges bromine for fluorine to give 2-fluorobutane ($\text{C}$).

Assertion (A): $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ occurs more readily than the $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$.
Reason (R): The partially bonded unhybridized $p$-orbital that develops in the trigonal bipyramidal transition state is stabilized by conjugation with the phenyl ring.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Benzyl bromide undergoes $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ substitution significantly faster than ethyl bromide because in the pentacoordinate trigonal bipyramidal transition state, the partially bonded $p$-orbital on the benzylic carbon overlaps with the $\pi$-electron cloud of the adjacent phenyl ring, lowering the activation energy. Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

question_text: In the reaction of $(1R, 2S)\text{-1-bromo-2-(4-methoxyphenyl)cyclohexane}$ (or *trans*-2-(4-methoxyphenyl)cyclohexyl bromide) with $\text{KCN}$ (or $\text{NaCN}$), the major product '$\text{P}$' is:

explanation: Statement I is correct because chloromethyl methyl ether ionises readily via $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ to form a resonance-stabilised oxocarbenium ion ($\text{CH}_3-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2^+ \leftrightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{O}^+=\text{CH}_2$). Statement II is correct because neopentyl chloride ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{Cl}$) suffers severe steric hindrance from the bulky *tert*-butyl group blocking backside $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ attack.

question_text: When *sec*-butylcyclohexane reacts with bromine in the presence of sunlight, the major product is:
explanation: Photobromination proceeds selectively at the most substituted tertiary carbon to form the most stable $3^\circ$ radical intermediate, giving (2-bromobutan-2-yl)cyclohexane as the major product (official key: C).

The maximum number of $\text{RBr}$ producing 2-methylbutane by the above sequence of reactions is ______ (Consider the structural isomers only):

(A) 3-bromocyclohex-1-ene
