question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The conversion proceeds well in the less polar medium:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl} + \text{OH}^- \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH} + \text{Cl}^-$
Statement II: The conversion proceeds well in the more polar medium:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl} + \text{R}_3\text{N} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{N}^+\text{R}_3\text{Cl}^-$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
explanation: According to the Hughes-Ingold rules: in Reaction I, a negatively charged nucleophile ($\text{OH}^-$) reacts with a neutral substrate, dispersing charge in the transition state ($[\text{HO}^{\delta-}\cdots\text{R}\cdots\text{Cl}^{\delta-}]$), so a less polar medium favours the reaction (Statement I is true). In Reaction II, two neutral reactants form separated charges in the transition state ($[\text{R}_3\text{N}^{\delta+}\cdots\text{R}\cdots\text{Cl}^{\delta-}]$), so a more polar medium stabilises the transition state and accelerates the reaction (Statement II is true).

question_text: The structure of the major product formed in the reaction of 1-bromo-4-(1-chloroethyl)benzene with $\text{AgCN}$ is:
explanation: Covalent $\text{AgCN}$ reacts selectively at the benzylic/aliphatic $\text{C}(sp^3)-\text{Cl}$ bond via nitrogen attack to form an isocyanide ($-\text{NC}$), whereas the aryl $\text{C}(sp^2)-\text{Br}$ bond is inert to nucleophilic substitution, giving 1-bromo-4-(1-isocyanoethyl)benzene.

question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\text{Et}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ will undergo alkaline hydrolysis at a faster rate than $\text{Et}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ (or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$).
Statement II: In $\text{Et}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$, intramolecular substitution takes place first by $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{i}$ involving lone pair of electrons on nitrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
explanation: In 2-chloro-$N,N$-diethylethan-1-amine ($\text{Et}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$), the nitrogen lone pair performs rapid neighbouring group participation (intramolecular nucleophilic displacement) to form a strained 3-membered aziridinium ion intermediate, which is quickly opened by $\text{OH}^-$ to give the alcohol much faster than simple bimolecular hydrolysis. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

question_text:
The products $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ in the following reactions, respectively are:
$\text{A} \xleftarrow{\text{AgNO}_2} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{AgCN}} \text{B}$
explanation: Both $\text{AgNO}_2$ and $\text{AgCN}$ are covalent silver salts in which the $\text{Ag}-\text{O}$ and $\text{Ag}-\text{C}$ bonds are not ionised, so nucleophilic substitution occurs through the lone pair on the nitrogen atom in both cases, yielding 1-nitropropane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NO}_2$, $\text{A}$) and propyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$, $\text{B}$).

question_text: The correct order of reactivity of $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ in methanol with the following nucleophiles is $\text{F}^-, \text{I}^-, \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$ and $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$:
explanation: In a polar protic solvent (methanol), nucleophilicity increases down a group as solvation decreases ($\text{I}^-$ is large, polarisable, and weakly solvated, whereas small $\text{F}^-$ is tightly caged by hydrogen bonding). Between the oxygen nucleophiles, strongly basic $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$ is more nucleophilic than resonance-stabilised $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}^-$. Hence, $\text{I}^- > \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^- > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O}^- > \text{F}^-$.

(II) 1-bromobicyclo[2.2.2]octane
(III) 2-bromopropane
(IV) (bromodiphenylmethyl)benzene ($\text{Ph}_3\text{CBr}$)
explanation: Bridgehead halides (I) and (II) cannot form planar carbocations due to Bredt's rule and are least reactive, with (I) slightly more reactive than (II) due to the $+\text{I}$ effect of the methyl group. Secondary 2-bromopropane (III) reacts faster than bridgehead halides, and triphenylmethyl bromide (IV) forms the extensively resonance-stabilised trityl carbocation ($\text{Ph}_3\text{C}^+$), reacting fastest. Thus, $(\text{II}) < (\text{I}) < (\text{III}) < (\text{IV})$.

Thus, B, C and E Only.
